3a4dd43fc4.why: Old dead lure (hardness) is gone. 'What kind of rock it is' is a live, truly wrong lure: mass alone cannot name a rock (a chip and a chunk of one rock differ). Key true (Grokipedia Mass: 'a quantitative measure of the amount of matter in an object'; balances compare with standard masses). Volume and density lures stay wrong. No tell, voice clean.

cdf0199023.why: Re-keyed to the rule itself; the stem shows no outcomes, so no lure is ruled out (its four objects even make the 'hard things sink' lure look right). The three lures are the Science Learning Hub's documented alternative conceptions (weight, size, soft objects float). Key true (Grokipedia Buoyancy: specific gravity under 1 floats, over 1 sinks). Context's 'lighter for its size' is now true even of green pine (0.70-0.91 of water), and ordinary stone is 2.2-3.0. The key's 'for its size' joins the words of two lures, a mild pattern, but it is the grade's own phrasing and the choices are parallel.

ce54252946.why: Dead stopwatch lure replaced by the string method, which is truly wrong (a length, not a volume, for a jagged shape). Key true (Grokipedia Displacement: a stone sunk in a measuring cylinder raises the level by its volume); 50 to 65 mL = 15 mL = 15 cubic cm. Note for the lead: the judge's optional 'better still' (all four choices using the cylinder) was not taken, so a child who knows only that a graduated cylinder goes with volume can still reach the key; the displacement idea is the grade's fact and is in the key, so this is not a fail.

c909474c14.why: No longer a twin of the particle unit's dissolving item: it now keys identification by solubility. Key true: salt dissolves (360 g per kg at 25 C), quartz sand is effectively insoluble (6-14 mg per litre). Each lure truly shows no difference: salt is diamagnetic (-1.4e-5) and sand is not pulled (NZCER Level 3 task: only the iron attaches); dry solid salt does not conduct (ions fixed) and silica is an insulator; salt melts at 800.7 C and silica near 1,710 C. 'At all' is gone from the context. Voice clean. Lead note: the mixtures-and-solutions draft's salt-and-sand filter item also turns on salt dissolving and sand not, though it keys separation, not identification.

d245a0db27.why: Error fixed: the partly true 'makes heat of its own' lure is now 'It keeps making heat, like a heater', which is wrong (Grokipedia Wool ties its small heat of sorption only to taking up water vapour, never steady heating), and the context no longer says the hat makes no heat. 'Chilly' dropped, as the judge asked. Key true (crimp traps still air; insulation slows heat flow). The stored-heat and soaks-up-warmth lures stay wrong (the hat and the air are cooler than her head), and the context does not mention damp wool next to them.

7546383462.why: The structural tell is gone: the four choices are the four combinations, each half twice. The 'as hard as steel' contradiction is gone. Key true (Grokipedia Mohs: fingernail about 2.5, pocket knife blade 5.5; a mineral scratches only lower ranks). The new lure is the scratch rule read backwards (M9). A child who knows steel is harder than a fingernail can see it is impossible, but it still catches the backwards reading the judge wanted, so it is not dead.
